drafter.message_to_opposing_counsel:
Thank you for your prompt response. We appreciate your client's consideration of the proposed Rent. To move this forward, the Landlord is prepared to reduce the monthly Base Rent to USD 82,000. We trust this reflects good faith toward an agreement, and look forward to your client's confirmation.

Regarding property taxes and operating expenses, we are agreeable to the Landlord remaining responsible, subject to customary carve-outs (e.g., for Tenant-specific costs or extraordinary assessments). We await your suggested language on these items as well as the standard clauses mentioned. Please advise if you would like us to circulate draft language for review.

probe.private_reasoning: The initial proposed Base Rent was USD 95,000/month, quickly reduced to USD 82,000/month in 'good faith,' a swift and significant drop (over 13%). This strong early concession — paired with language about hoping for 'confirmation' — suggests USD 82,000 is not their minimum. The deal framing (Landlord remains responsible for taxes/ops expenses, only standard carve-outs) indicates further economic flexibility. Their comments and drafting reveal no hidden term or exception on this, and there are no tracked changes resisting further rent adjustment. They signaled eagerness for speedy agreement and did not mark USD 82,000 as 'final.' It is likely their true minimum is lower, probably in the high 70s (USD 75,000–78,000).
